svg.title: FINN: public filings read once for everyone; your side below a line, touched only by code; your phone outside both sides, getting public facts and only what's yours
svg.desc: Solid parts run in this repo today; dashed parts are designed, not built yet. Above a line is the public side. Everything companies file with the stock exchange (NSE) and each day's prices, fetched by hand for now with a year kept, become events: one per filing, saved once, with a new version only if a key detail changes. They are then read and checked: rules sort most filings, an AI model reads the rest once it is given a key, and code checks what it read. What comes out is facts, what FINN keeps from each filing: how urgent it is, how big it is next to the company's revenue, what results it reports and who it names. A price study looks back over the year and asks whether the stock moved after a filing FINN would alert you to; it tests the alert rules and never changes what the app shows you. Answering a question searches a company's own calls with investors and quotes what it finds; an AI model sees your question only if it can't train on it, never with your name or holdings, and FINN doesn't keep the question; the app has no screen for this yet. The app's snapshot, built by hand on 28 Oct from NSE and screener.in, is what the app shows, and the app can fetch one company live when you ask; building the snapshot from the facts is designed. Below the line is your side, touched only by code and never by a model: what you hold and who you know, both invented for this demo, matched to the public facts by code, inside a locked space of its own in the cloud that is designed; the one read-only copy of public facts into it is designed too. Your phone sits outside both sides and gets public facts from the snapshot and, as designed, only what's yours. For production, not deployed (ADR 5): Google Cloud, with events and facts in Cloud SQL, reading and answering on Cloud Run and Vertex AI, and the private side locked so nothing in it can send data out, read by your phone only when signed in.
